newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ sees core inflation peaking at 2.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ sees core inflation peaking at 2.7 pct.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand on Friday forecast underlying annual inflation to peak at 2.7 percent in the September 1996 quarter.

In its six monthly economic projections, the bank forecast the inflation rate to then fall to 2.1 percent in the March 1997 year, 0.8 percent in the March 1998 year and to 0.5 percent the following year.

In its June Monetary Policy Statement, the bank forecast inflation would peak at 2.6 percent in the September 1996 year before easing back to 1.1 percent a year later and to 0.3 percent in the September 1998 year.
